claims.claim: [1] Proxy/TLS ease with operational visibility/recovery is a documented category pattern across independent NPM and Caddy UI maintainers [1,3,4,5]; no adoption inference.
[3] X4Applegate documents validation, rollback, TLS visibility, access control and fleet capabilities; not exercised or independently corroborated.
[4] zackwag documents Caddyfile-first editing with health, TLS, logs and recovery; not exercised.
[5] rhad00 documents broad proxy management, auth, operational features and automation; not exercised.
[6] Caddy manages HTTPS but local CA trust and persistent storage are deployment responsibilities; canonical documentation only.
[7] Scoped API with ETag guards exists; multirequest changes are not one transaction and adapt does not load config; canonical documentation only.
[8] API-oriented Caddy service uses resume and persisted autosave; canonical documentation only.
[9] DNS-01 enables wildcard and private-server certificate validation without inbound challenge ports; independent Caddy and Lets Encrypt docs agree.
[10] Native proxy supports WebSockets and upstream TLS controls; verification bypass removes protection; canonical documentation only.
[11] A user reported opaque save errors after an upgrade and reverting versions; one firsthand account, root cause not independently verified.
[12] A user reported opaque DNS certificate failure and difficulty locating logs, then a credential resolution; one firsthand account.
[13] A user reports renewed certificate not served until reload; not reproduced or confirmed as current bug.
[14] X4Applegate release page shows October activity; activity does not prove reliability or roadmap.
[15] zackwag release page shows October activity; activity does not prove reliability or roadmap.
